item.title: ‘Collision wins Tests’
item.description: THE Fijiana XVs are sharpening their physical game ahead of this weekend’s Test match against the Springbok Women, with interim head coach Mike Legge identifying the collision area as the team’s top priority. item.content:encoded:
THE Fijiana XVs are sharpening their physical game ahead of this weekend’s Test match against the Springbok Women, with interim head coach Mike Legge identifying the collision area as the team’s top priority.

The national side resumed training this week as players continued assembling in camp, giving the coaching staff time to fine-tune combinations before Saturday’s clash. Legge noted that lessons learned from their Super Rugby Women’s final defeat to the NSW Waratahs have directly shaped their preparations.

“Our big focus this week is the collision,” Legge said. “What we learnt from losing the final against the Waratahs was making sure we win the collision. South Africa is a big team. I don’t think the girls would have come up against a team the size of South Africa before.”

He acknowledged the stern test awaiting them on the pitch. “It’s going to be a massive, massive challenge for us,” he said.

While a few players are still expected to arrive in camp, the interim head coach expressed confidence that the squad will be fully prepared. He added that South Africa will provide a rigorous test after building momentum in recent international fixtures.

“They’ve had a good test series against the US, which was recent. They’re a team that’s slowly building in.

“These girls wouldn’t have come up against a size like that. Probably the physicality, but it’s going to be a good challenge for us.”

Despite the emphasis on matching South Africa’s size and power, Legge insisted Fiji will not stray from its signature flair.

“We want to continue our style of game,” Legge said.

“So, we’ll work hard on the collision, work hard on what we do on the edges as well. It’s going to be pretty much similar to how we played the last couple of months.”

Although a few squad members are currently on modified training programs following the Super Rugby Women’s final, they are expected to return to full training shortly.

“Some of our girls are still carrying some injuries from the Super final. So, they’re only doing some modified stuff today, but they’ll be back for training.”

With the Test taking place at HFC Bank Stadium in Suva, Legge is calling on local fans to turn out in full force.

“We have our core group of supporters that continue to follow us where we go. I know they’ll show up in numbers on Saturday, but also, we’re hoping that the Dean’s parents remain and support our girls as well. I think it’s going to be a really good game. Two very different styles of rugby.”

item.description: THE race for the Vodafone Super Deans Trophy has reached the knockout stage, with secondary schools across Fiji confirming their places in the national quarter-finals after another thrilling weekend of rugby action. item.content:encoded:
THE race for the Vodafone Super Deans Trophy has reached the knockout stage, with secondary schools across Fiji confirming their places in the national quarter-finals after another thrilling weekend of rugby action.

In the premier Under-18 grade, southern giants Suva Grammar School once again stamped their authority with a commanding playoff performance to secure a quarter-final berth. They will be joined by Nasinu Secondary School, who edged out their opponents in a hard-fought encounter to keep their title hopes alive.

• Under-14: Mahatma Gandhi Memorial School (MGM), Suva Grammar School (SGS), Nasinu Secondary School (NSS):

• Under-15: SGS, Marist Brothers High School (MBHS), NSS:

• Under-17: SGS, Gospel High School, MBHS:

• Under-19: SGS, NSS, Ratu Simione Matanitobua College

In the Eastern Division, unbeaten Lelean Memorial School continued its impressive campaign and will be joined by Ratu Kadavulevu School in the Under-18 national quarter-finals.

Queen Victoria School, Ratu Kadavulevu School and Lelean Memorial School also secured qualification in the Under-14, Under-15, Under-16 and Under-17 grades. In the Under-19 division, RKS and Lelean will be joined by Navatu Secondary School.

The Western Division celebrated a significant achievement, with four schools advancing to the Under-18 quarter-finals.

Ra High School, Ba Provincial Freebird Institute, Cuvu College and Ratu Navula College all booked their places after strong performances in the elimination round.

• Under-14: Ratu Navula College, Nadi Muslim College:

• Under-15: Natabua High: School, Ba Methodist High School

• Under-16: Cuvu College, Ratu Navula College:

• Under-17: Ba Methodist High School, Sigatoka Methodist College: and

• Under-19: Ratu Navula College, Xavier College.

Meanwhile, the Weet-Bix Raluve Championship Under-16 quarter-finals will feature Adi Cakobau School, St Vincent College, Bucalevu Secondary School, Nabala Secondary School, Nasinu Secondary School, Suva Grammar School, Sigatoka Methodist College and St Theresa’s High School.

The Weet-Bix Raluve Under-18 competition will include Sila Central High School, Adi Cakobau School, St Bedes College, Bucalevu Secondary School, Lomary Secondary School, Mahatma Gandhi Memorial School, defending champions Jasper Williams High School and last year’s runners-up Natabua High School.

With traditional powerhouses and emerging challengers still in contention, the stage is set for another electrifying weekend of schools rugby.

Every match now carries added significance as teams battle for a coveted place in the national semi-finals, with months of preparation and sacrifice on the line.

item.title: Wairabetia school claims back-to-back U14 soccer title
item.description: WAIRABETIA Muslim Primary School successfully defended its under-14 soccer title after producing an unbeaten campaign in the Tabua Grade at the Lautoka Inter-primary schools Soccer competition held at Central Primary Ground last weekend. Led by head boy and captain Napolioni Waqatabu, the young side showed determination and discipline to secure back-to-back championship honours.
item.content:encoded:
WAIRABETIA Muslim Primary School successfully defended its under-14 soccer title after producing an unbeaten campaign in the Tabua Grade at the Lautoka Inter-primary schools Soccer competition held at Central Primary Ground last weekend.

Led by head boy and captain Napolioni Waqatabu, the young side showed determination and discipline to secure back-to-back championship honours.

Wairabetia opened its campaign with two scoreless draws against Dreketi Sangam Primary and Tuvu Primary before finding its rhythm in the third match with a convincing 2-0 victory over Qalitu Primary. The goals came from Mateo Draunimasi of Year 8 and captain Waqatabu.

The semi-final proved to be another hard-fought contest as Wairabetia edged Satya Sai Primary 1-0. Goalkeeper Cama Veiqaravi emerged as the hero after producing a crucial penalty save, while Waqatabu scored the decisive goal to send his side into the final.

In the championship match, Wairabetia once again defeated Tuvu Primary 2-0 to lift the title. Waqatabu continued his outstanding form by finding the back of the net, while Year 6 student Isoa Musuqio added the second goal to seal the victory.

The team was guided by coach Imraan Iqbal, a former Fiji Football Association referee, whose experience played a key role in the school’s successful title defence.

Meanwhile, Wairabetia Muslim Primary’s under-14 girls also made an encouraging debut in the tournament, impressing against more experienced opponents. Goalkeeper Banikarawa Mita, who hails from Rabi, highlighted the team’s performance with a brilliant penalty save.

The girls were coached by Aachal Narayan, who praised the team’s effort and commitment throughout the competition.

Following their successful outing, Wairabetia Muslim Primary will now shift their focus to the Northwest Primary Schools Soccer Competition in Term Three, which will be held in Ba after the Fiji Year Eight Examination, where both teams will be eager to continue building on their strong performances.

item.title: Runners-uptag pleases coach Naidu
item.description: TUVU Primary School’s under-14 coach Navnil Naidu is proud of his players’ efforts after they finished as runners-up in the Tabua Grade at the Lautoka Inter-primary Schools Soccer Competition held at the Central Primary School ground last weekend. Naidu said the achievement was a positive sign of the school’s growing football program, especially for the girls’ team which has now secured runners-up
item.content:encoded:
TUVU Primary School’s under-14 coach Navnil Naidu is proud of his players’ efforts after they finished as runners-up in the Tabua Grade at the Lautoka Inter-primary Schools Soccer Competition held at the Central Primary School ground last weekend.

Naidu said the achievement was a positive sign of the school’s growing football program, especially for the girls’ team which has now secured runners-up honours for three consecutive years.

“I’m very happy with the performance. Three years ago, we introduced soccer for the girls and for the past three years we have been runners-up. This is the third year in a row,” Naidu said.

He said the boys also showed great commitment after reaching the final for the first time in many years.

“The boys were focused and their mindset was very good. Their fighting spirit was excellent. When we defeated last year’s champions Drasa Sangam by two goals in the pool stages, that’s where the boys clicked.”

Naidu said attention would now turn to the selection of players for the Lautoka under-14 district team, with talented players attracting interest from selectors.

He acknowledged the support from the school management, headteacher and his wife Shania Naidu, who managed both teams during the tournament.

Naidu also highlighted the importance of grassroots development, saying football growth begins at primary school level.

However, he called for more support for smaller schools facing limited resources and urged organisers to consider holding future tournaments on school days to allow all students to participate.

item.title: ‘Blacks’ eye EPL title
item.description: THE journey back to the top has been built on belief, patience and unity, and now Dayals Sawmillers Ba FC stands just one victory away from lifting the 2026 Extra Premier League title. After edging Labasa FC 2-1 in a crucial encounter last Saturday, the Men in Black moved within touching distance of another major achievement, adding to the Fiji FACT title they claimed earlier this season.
item.content:encoded:
THE journey back to the top has been built on belief, patience and unity, and now Dayals Sawmillers Ba FC stands just one victory away from lifting the 2026 Extra Premier League title.

After edging Labasa FC 2-1 in a crucial encounter last Saturday, the Men in Black moved within touching distance of another major achievement, adding to the Fiji FACT title they claimed earlier this season.

For Ba FC president Praneel Dayal, the hard-fought win in Labasa was about much more than three competition points.

“Some victories are about more than football. Celebrating the win in Labasa alongside my son, Aanav Dayal, made the moment even more meaningful. Sharing the joy with family, our players and every Ba supporter is something I’ll always treasure.

“Proud to be Ba. Proud to celebrate together. We are Ba!”

Behind the celebrations are years of commitment to rebuilding one of Fiji football’s most successful clubs and Dayal has played a key role in guiding Ba back into title contention, backing the team through difficult periods and helping restore the winning culture the district is renowned for.

Now, with only Tailevu Naitasiri standing between Ba and the league trophy, the focus remains firmly on finishing the job.

“We look forward to a good game against Tailevu Naitasiri this week. If we win that, we lift the title,” Dayal said.

Across the soccer-mad town of Ba, excitement continues to grow with supporters who have stood by the club through every challenge hoping to witness another memorable chapter in the district’s proud football history.

Having already captured the Fiji FACT crown, Ba FC now has the opportunity to complete a remarkable campaign by adding the Extra Premier League title to its trophy cabinet. One more win would not only reward the players and officials for their dedication throughout the season but also give the loyal Ba faithful another reason to celebrate.

For a club built on tradition and success, the trophy is now in sight. The final step remains, and the Men in Black know that history is theirs to write.

item.title: Kadavu’s debut at Skipper Cup
item.description: Kadavu Rugby head coach Solomone Nute believes the team’s maiden Skipper Cup campaign is an important learning journey as the island side looks to improve after their opening match of the Skipper Cup against Nadi last weekend. Nute said the team’s performance showed promising signs despite mistakes on the field, with the players gaining valuable experience against more established opposition.
item.content:encoded:
Kadavu Rugby head coach Solomone Nute believes the team’s maiden Skipper Cup campaign is an important learning journey as the island side looks to improve after their opening match of the Skipper Cup against Nadi last weekend.

Nute said the team’s performance showed promising signs despite mistakes on the field, with the players gaining valuable experience against more established opposition.

“First of all, we thank God Almighty. This is our development and our growth,” Nute said.

“This is our first-time here as a baby of the Skipper Cup Competition since this is our debut to the competition this year. This group of boys, they come from the village, and we are trying to develop them from the village to bridge the gap from the Vanua Cup Championship to the Skipper Cup Competition.”

Nute said the team would return to the drawing board to analyse their performance and correct areas that need improvement.

“I think, in my heart, we are playing well. We are going back to our drawing board, learn from our mistakes and learn from that,” he said.

Nute added that the challenge for Kadavu is building consistency as they adjust to the intensity and demands of top-level provincial rugby.

The islanders will now shift their focus to their next assignment against Naitasiri at Ratu Cakobau Park in Nausori this Saturday.

“We still have to go back and review our game. I know there are some problems, but we can’t do that. We have to work on them,” Nute said.

The coach also acknowledged the important role played by their supporters in helping the team make history in their first Skipper Cup season.

“We thank our supporters, the supporters that built this and brought us here,” he added.

Kadavu will be aiming to turn lessons from their opening match into improvements as they continue their historic Skipper Cup journey.

item.title: Nadi shows resilience in opener
item.description: THE McDonald’s Nadi side showed composure in their 19-15 win against Kadavu in the opening round of the 2026 Skipper Cup competition at King Charles Park last Saturday. Nadi head coach Cohan Politini said his players remained committed to their game plan and displayed the mental strength needed to secure an important first-round win.
item.content:encoded:
THE McDonald’s Nadi side showed composure in their 19-15 win against Kadavu in the opening round of the 2026 Skipper Cup competition at King Charles Park last Saturday.

Nadi head coach Cohan Politini said his players remained committed to their game plan and displayed the mental strength needed to secure an important first-round win.

“We knew the first game was always going to be the toughest, especially with all the hype surrounding the match against Kadavu,” Politini said.

“There was extra pressure, but we tried to shut that out and stick to our processes. We were rattled a few times by Kadavu, but thanks to the boys’ mental capacity, they came back and managed to hold it together until the end.”

“The impact players made a difference. We managed to bring them on at the right time, and we’re grateful to have a strong bench that came in and made the difference.”

Nadi fielded a youthful outfit featuring seven debutants, with many players graduating from last year’s Under-20 squad. The coach was encouraged by the way the newcomers handled the physicality and pressure of senior provincial rugby.

“They did very well, especially those who came off the bench. We look forward to using them more during the season.”

While pleased with the result, he acknowledged there was plenty of work ahead before Nadi’s second-round clash against Lautoka.

“Our set pieces need improvement. It’s only the first game, so we have to get our systems right, improve our execution and be more accurate with our intentions. If we continue to improve, we should progress gradually throughout the season.”

He also admitted the large contingent of Kadavu supporters created a challenging atmosphere but said his players remained focused.

“They had the majority of the support, but we tried not to let that affect us and just played our game.”

Politini thanked the Nadi supporters for their backing and expressed confidence that the side can continue building momentum throughout the Skipper Cup season.

item.title: Determine to deliver | Building a strong relation with players: Mooar
item.description: NEW Swire Shipping Fijian Drua head coach Brad Mooar says building strong relationships with players and creating an environment where they want to stay will be central to his leadership. Mooar, who officially begins his role in September, said he was attracted to the Drua by its people, culture and the opportunity to work with talented Fijian athletes.
item.content:encoded:
NEW Swire Shipping Fijian Drua head coach Brad Mooar says building strong relationships with players and creating an environment where they want to stay will be central to his leadership.

Mooar, who officially begins his role in September, said he was attracted to the Drua by its people, culture and the opportunity to work with talented Fijian athletes.

“What attracted me is the people, the culture, and the opportunity to work with some outstanding athletes in the game that we love as well,” Mooar said.

Mooar said his leadership would be built around caring for players as individuals, understanding their lives outside rugby and respecting what is important to them.

He said faith was an important part of Fijian culture and would be embraced within the Drua environment.

“The vision, or certainly how I lead, is we care for our people, care for them as individuals and as the people that they are, get to know them, understand what life is outside of here, who’s in your family, who’s important to you, why do you play, care for the faith, it’s very important in Fijian people in particular, and to show that we respect that and embrace and show our belief and care in that space,” he said.

Mooar said players would also be valued and empowered to contribute their individual strengths to the team.

“Value, we value our people, we value them as individuals that they are and value what they do here, show them how important it is what they do for us and to achieve what we do and then empower them.

“Empower the individual to have the space to bring what they want to bring to our group.”

Mooar believes the Drua already has a strong foundation, crediting the work of former coaches Mick Byrne and Glen Jackson.

Rather than making wholesale changes, he wants to build on the strengths already within the squad.

“We have wonderful athletes, strong, fast, skilful, powerful athletes.

“What we need to do is to make sure we bring them together to give them real clarity of role, clarity of what we’re about as a team and then that allows them to bring their skill sets to the fore in every game and take the opportunities that are in front of them.”

Mooar identified a strong set piece and aggressive defence as key areas for the Drua, while maintaining the attacking flair the team is known for.

“I think ensuring that we have a really strong set piece and an aggressive, strong defence that is built on defending our people, defending our village will be key roles for us to get right going forward to add to the attacking flair and the attacking ability that we’ve got,” he said.

Mooar’s key performance indicator is whether players finish the season wanting to remain part of the Drua.

“My biggest KPI for 2027 is that we have a group of people, everyone that has been part of the Drua by the end of the season wants to stay.

“That they’ve had an experience that inspires them, excites them, that has improved them, challenged them and has been absolutely enjoyable in the good times and in the challenging times.”

Mooar brings experience from coaching environments including the Crusaders, All Blacks and Scotland.

He said those experiences had taught him the importance of adapting to new environments, listening and understanding the culture before trying to make changes.

“I believe that every environment you go into, you’re the visitor. This is the Drua environment, the Fiji environment, that I’m now privileged to be part of.

“I need to fit and contribute into this environment, not the other way around,” he added.

As he prepares to officially begin in September, Mooar said Drua players could expect a demanding but enjoyable environment where effort would be non-negotiable.

“They can expect to enjoy being here, to enjoy coming to work, bounce out of bed to get to the Drua and work hard for each other.

“They’ll know that effort is a compulsory requirement. We all work hard physically, mentally, emotionally. We will put in the effort for each other and that will drive performance.”

Mooar also promised an environment where players could have fun, laugh and sing while working towards a common goal.

To the Drua supporters, Mooar had a simple message.

“We’re thrilled to be here, thank you for the opportunity, thank you for supporting our team, loving the game and for the opportunity, it’s just magnificent.

“We can’t wait to get to work and look forward to meeting everyone,” he concluded.
